peek.sealed.kid: Locked: this box can’t read it.
peek.sealed.nerd: Encrypted: this hop can’t read it.
peek.role.start.kid: {hop} writes the message and packs it into envelopes, one inside the other.
peek.role.start.nerd: The sender builds the packet: each layer adds its header around the one inside.
peek.role.end.kid: Arrived! {hop} opens every envelope, one by one.
peek.role.end.nerd: Destination: each layer is checked and taken off, all the way up to the application.
peek.role.bridge.kid: {hop} swaps the outer envelope and passes the parcel on. It doesn’t read the address.
peek.role.bridge.nerd: {hop} bridges: it reads and rewrites only the link layer; the IP packet passes untouched.
peek.role.router.kid: {hop} reads the address and picks the best way onwards.
peek.role.router.nerd: Routed: longest-prefix match on the destination, TTL − 1, an ECMP hash over the 5-tuple, and a new link frame.
peek.role.switched.kid: {hop} reads only the motorway sticker and swaps it for the next one. It doesn’t even look at the address.
peek.role.switched.nerd: Label-switched: the top label is swapped and the MPLS TTL counted down; the IP header inside isn’t read.
peek.role.nat.up.kid: {hop} swaps the sender address for its own outside address, and remembers who asked.
peek.role.nat.up.nerd: NAT: the source is rewritten to the outside address, checksums are fixed and the mapping is kept; then it’s routed (TTL − 1).
peek.role.nat.down.kid: {hop} looks up who asked for this and changes the address back.
peek.role.nat.down.nerd: NAT reverse: the destination is rewritten back from the mapping table, checksums fixed, then routed (TTL − 1).
peek.role.passive.kid: {hop} doesn’t open a thing: it just passes the signal on, with no power at all.
peek.role.passive.nerd: {hop} is passive: no power and no electronics. It reads no bits; it only splits the signal and passes it on.

about.countWhat: Each time the app opens, it sends one count with its language to the author's own stats server: no cookie, no ID. The server sees your IP address like any site, uses it only for your country, and keeps only totals, which are published.
about.countDnt: Your browser asks sites not to track you, so your visits aren't counted.
